label: Credit unit 'helper tool' (understated framing)
brief: Registering a small helper tool for the central credit unit. FinScore Retail gives our credit officers a quick summary view of each applicant's file so they can work faster. The officers stay fully in charge of every case. It was built in-house by credit risk analytics, it does not generate content, and nobody outside the unit sees it. The Head of Consumer Finance owns it.

label: WhatsApp FAQ assistant (complete brief)
brief: We would like to register an AI use case. It is called AskAmana. The Head of Customer Service owns it. We built it on a third-party large language model API. The model is a commercial LLM accessed through an API provider. In production on WhatsApp. It answers customers' questions about our products, fees and branch timings on WhatsApp, using only our published product documents. It does not take decisions; it answers questions and hands over to a human agent for account-specific requests. Customer service. It must not give account-specific, financial or Shariah rulings advice. Customers use it directly; the digital service team manages it. Customers and members of the public who message us on WhatsApp. Yes, it chats with individual customers, but it takes no decisions about them. About 80,000 conversations a month. Elderly and low-literacy customers; it offers a human agent at any time. No output is used in the EU and no affected people are in the EU. It answers on its own without human review of each answer. Customer questions and our published product documents. Customers' phone numbers and messages, which are personal data. It uses no biometric data. It is a pre-trained model; we do not train it, we ground it on our documents. Messages go to the model provider's API in the United States under a zero-retention agreement. A large language model with retrieval over our documents. Yes, it generates text answers. Yes, customers chat with it directly on WhatsApp. Reads from the product document store; writes chat transcripts to the CRM. On 500 test questions it answered 91% correctly and refused 6% appropriately. We red-teamed it with 300 prompt-injection and abuse prompts. Answers are grounded only on approved documents, an output filter blocks account advice and abusive content, and every answer cites a document. Weekly accuracy sampling and a monthly hallucination review. Digital service can switch WhatsApp to human agents immediately. The first message tells customers they are talking to an AI assistant. The API provider was assessed by IT risk; the contract covers zero retention and incident notice. SBP cloud outsourcing and consumer protection rules apply.

label: Developer coding assistant (brief with gaps)
brief: Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called DevPilot. The Chief Technology Officer owns it. It is a third-party coding assistant built on a large language model API. A commercial AI coding assistant provider. In production for the IT department. It suggests code completions and explains code to our software developers inside their editor. Internal productivity for software development. Only our developers use it; no customers are affected directly. No, it does not produce outputs about people. It only suggests code; developers decide. Source code and developer prompts; no customer data. It uses no biometric data. Pre-trained by the provider; our code is not used for training under the contract. Provider's cloud in the United States; code snippets are not retained. Large language model for code. Developers interact with it in their editor. Integrated into developer editors; it cannot change production systems. Developers accept about 30% of suggestions; security scans show no increase in vulnerabilities. Secrets scanning blocks credentials in prompts; static analysis runs on all code. Code review, static analysis and a licence filter for suggested code. Quarterly review of usage and security scan results. IT can revoke licences immediately. IT risk assessed the provider and the contract excludes training on our code. SBP technology risk and cloud outsourcing frameworks.

label: Contact-centre 'wellbeing' tool (understated framing)
brief: Registering a staff wellbeing tool for the contact centre. VoicePulse is a vendor SaaS product that helps team leaders support agents who may be having a hard day, by highlighting calls where an agent sounded under pressure. Team leaders use it to start supportive coaching conversations. It runs in the background on call recordings and does not generate any content. The Head of Contact Centre Operations owns it and it is in a three-month pilot.

label: Card fraud auto-block (brief with gaps)
brief: Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called CardShield. The Head of Fraud Risk owns it. It is a vendor fraud platform. A global payments fraud vendor. In production. It scores every debit and credit card transaction for fraud in real time. Fraud detection. Not for credit decisions or AML reporting. The fraud operations team. Cardholders and the merchants they pay. About 4 million transactions a month. Elderly customers abroad are more often blocked; they can call the 24-hour line. Cardholders sometimes travel in the EU but no output is used there by us. High-risk transactions are declined and cards blocked automatically without human review. Fraud operations review blocked cards within 30 minutes during business hours and can unblock them. Customers can call the 24-hour helpline to confirm the transaction and unblock the card. Transaction details, merchant data, device and location data. Personal financial data. It uses no biometric data. Vendor cloud in Singapore. Vendor neural network fraud model. It does not generate any text, image or other content. Nobody interacts with it directly; it runs in the background. Reads card authorisations from the card switch and writes decline and block instructions back to it. Fraud detection rate of 72% at a false-positive ratio of 8 to 1. We have checked block rates by age band; customers over 65 are blocked 1.4 times more often. Top risk factors per alert. Vendor is PCI DSS certified and pen-tested. Daily fraud and false-positive dashboards; monthly model review with the vendor. We can switch to rules-only mode within minutes. All scores and decisions are logged for seven years. Customers receive an SMS when a transaction is declined. Full vendor due diligence and an SBP-compliant outsourcing contract. A data protection impact assessment was completed. SBP cloud outsourcing framework and payment card rules apply.

label: SME company credit score (edge case)
brief: We would like to register an AI use case. It is called SMEScore. The Head of SME Banking owns it. Built in-house. In production. It scores the credit risk of incorporated companies, private limited companies only, applying for working capital financing, from their audited financial statements. SME relationship managers and the credit committee use the score when deciding company financing. SME and corporate lending to companies. SME credit analysts. Incorporated companies applying for financing. No, it scores companies, not individuals. It recommends; the credit committee decides. Audited financial statements, company bureau data and account conduct. No personal data; company data only. It uses no biometric data. Eight years of SME financing outcomes. Onshore. Logistic regression scorecard. It does not generate any text, image or other content. Nobody interacts with it directly; it runs in the background. Reads from the credit workflow; writes scores back. Gini 0.60. Tested on missing financials. Quarterly validation. Analysts revert to the manual rating. SBP prudential regulations for SME financing.

label: CV 'sorting assistant' (understated framing)
brief: Registering TalentRank, a sorting assistant inside our vendor applicant tracking system. It simply organises the incoming CV pile for our recruiters so they can work through it faster; recruiters remain in full control of hiring. It does not generate content and candidates never interact with it. Owned by the Head of Talent Acquisition.
